S6.01.note: Colour tokens are defined in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; the effect is seen by switching Theme.
steps: Open Settings… from the Mac menu bar (AGI app menu) or press Cmd+,.
Go to Appearance and click Light, then Dark, then System under Theme.
Compare the page and panel backgrounds in each theme with Expected.

S6.02.note: Raised-surface token is set in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; no visible control of its own.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Switch Theme between Light and Dark.
Compare cards, menus and dialogs with the page background in each theme; open a menu or the Settings dialog itself to see the raised surface.

S6.03.note: Text tokens are in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; contrast is verified by apps/web/shared/components/__tests__/theme-contrast.test.ts, not by a person.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Switch Theme to Light, then Dark.
Read primary and muted text in chat and settings in each theme and compare with Expected.

S6.04.note: Subtle and strong border tokens are in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; no separate control.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Switch Theme between Light and Dark.
Look at card edges, dividers and input borders in Settings > General and compare with Expected.

S6.05.note: Fill, text and on-fill roles are in CSS tokens; the swatch names come from apps/web/content/support/chat-basics.md.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Click a colour under Accent colour (AGI amber, Green, Blue, Violet or Rose).
Look at selected controls and buttons, and check the text on them is readable, against Expected.

S6.06.note: Status colours are tokens in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css; no single visible control, so the tester must find a screen that shows a status.
steps: Trigger a status message, for example a failed or warning state, in the chat or settings.
Compare the success, warning, error or info text colour in Light and Dark Theme.

S6.07.note: Font families are declared in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/chat.css and apps/web/app/globals.css.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Click Chat font and pick Sans, Serif or Dyslexic friendly.
Look at message text in a chat; code should stay monospace.

S6.08.note: The heading scale is in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/tailwind.css; no control of its own.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Compare the page title Appearance with the row labels such as Theme and Motion.

S6.09.note: Default is shown as Default in the options list.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Choose Small, then Large under Chat text size.
Look at chat message text and compare with Default and Expected.

S6.10.note: The caption role is defined in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/tailwind.css; no single control of its own.
steps: Open a chat and look at small metadata text such as timestamps or hint text under a Settings row, for example the hint under Contrast.

S6.11.needs: a chat that contains a code block
S6.11.note: Monospace family is declared in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/chat.css; the support page says code stays monospace.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Set Chat font to Serif, then return to Default.
Open a chat with a code block and compare the code text with the body text.

S6.12.needs: a chat reply with several lines
S6.12.note: Line-height is set per text role in apps/web/app/globals.css; no control of its own.
steps: Read a multi-line chat reply and compare line spacing between lines of the same paragraph and in headings.

S6.13.needs: a chat reply with several paragraphs
S6.13.note: Paragraph gap is set in apps/web/app/globals.css; no control of its own.
steps: Ask for a reply with several paragraphs in a chat.
Look at the vertical gap between paragraphs and compare with Expected.

S6.14.needs: a chat reply with a list
S6.14.note: List indentation is set in apps/web/app/globals.css; no control of its own.
steps: Ask for a reply containing a bulleted or numbered list, with a nested item.
Look at the indent of the list and the nested list.

S6.15.needs: a chat that contains a code block with a long line
S6.15.note: Padding itself is set in apps/web/app/globals.css; the toggle only changes wrapping.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to Appearance.
Turn on Wrap long code lines, then turn it off.
Open a chat with a long code line and look at the code block padding and whether the line wraps.
S6.15.where: Settings… (Cmd+,) > Appearance > Wrap long code lines

S6.16.needs: a chat reply with a table
S6.16.note: Table-cell padding is applied in the shared layout rules; no control of its own.
steps: Open a chat reply or a data table that contains a table.
Compare the padding inside table cells.

S6.17.note: Turn spacing is set in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx; no control of its own.
steps: Send two or more messages in one chat.
Look at the vertical space between one turn and the next.

S6.18.note: Spacing is in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/messageActionRow.ts; the toolbar appears on hover.
steps: Hover over a chat message to show its action toolbar.
Look at the distance between the message and its toolbar.

S6.19.note: Composer padding is in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx; no control of its own.
steps: Open a chat and click into the message box at the bottom.
Look at the space around the typed text and the send and attach controls.

S6.20.needs: a window that can be resized
S6.20.note: Gutters are in apps/web/app/globals.css and apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; visible through window resize.
steps: Open a chat page and resize the window width from wide to narrow.
Look at the space between the page edge and the content.

S6.21.needs: a few chats in the sidebar
S6.21.note: Row height is set in packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/SessionItem.tsx; no control of its own.
steps: Open the sidebar and look at a row of the chat history list.
Look at the height of several rows and compare them.

S6.22.note: Menu item height is in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/DropdownMenu.tsx; no control of its own.
steps: Click a menu button, for example the menu on a chat row in the sidebar.
Compare the height of the menu items with the other menus.

S6.23.note: Dialog padding is set in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Dialog.tsx and AlertDialog.tsx.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and look at the inner padding of the dialog.
Open a confirmation dialog, for example a delete prompt, and compare its inner padding.

S6.24.note: Spacing is set in the shared FieldRow component; no separate control.
steps: Open Settings… (Cmd+,) and go to General.
Look at the Full name label and its input under Profile.
Look at the gap between the label and the input and between fields, and compare with Expected.

S6.25.note: Icon grid and stroke are set in packages/ui/icons/src/grid.ts and CreateIcon.tsx; no control of its own.
steps: Look at the icons in the sidebar and in the settings navigation.
Compare the stroke weight and size of icons across rows.

S6.26.note: Button sizes (xs, sm, default, lg, icon) are set in code by the Button primitive, and a tester cannot pick one. Checked packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx.
S6.26.where: No control of its own. Button sizes show as buttons of different heights and widths across the app, for example in Settings.

S6.27.note: Not in this range. Outside S6.26 to S6.35, so not handled.

S6.28.note: Not in this range. Outside S6.26 to S6.35, so not handled.

S6.29.note: Layer values come from named z-index tokens in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css (--z-control, --z-modal); the dialog uses var(--z-modal) in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Dialog.tsx.
steps: Click the button whose name starts with Account menu for.
Click Settings in the menu.
Look: the Settings dialog sits above the chat and the sidebar, and the menu closes.
S6.29.where: No control. Its effect shows when menus and dialogs open over the chat and sidebar.

S6.30.note: Named durations are in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/foundation.css (--duration-instant 90ms, --duration-quick 160ms, --duration-moved 260ms). Sheets use them in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Sheet.tsx.
steps: Click the button whose name starts with Account menu for and watch the menu open.
Click Settings and watch the Settings dialog open.
Look: the menu opens and closes with a short fade, and the dialog fades and slides in without a long pause.
S6.30.where: No control. Its effect shows in how fast menus and dialogs open and close.

S6.31.needs: none (optional: to test the OS setting, turn on Reduce motion in macOS System Settings > Accessibility > Display)
S6.31.note: The in-app Motion switch sets data-motion=reduced (apps/web/shared/components/AppearancePreferences.tsx); the OS setting uses prefers-reduced-motion in apps/web/app/globals.css. Only System and Reduced exist; there is no full-motion option.
steps: Click the app menu, then Settings…, or press Command+,.
Click Appearance in the left list.
Find the row labelled Motion and click Reduced.
Look: the Motion row shows Reduced as pressed, and looping or moving animation in the chat and interface stops or becomes gentle. Click System to return.
S6.31.where: Settings… > Appearance > Motion > Reduced (Settings… is in the app menu on the Mac)

S6.32.needs: none (for System: access to macOS System Settings > Appearance)
S6.32.note: The Electron side follows the choice through nativeTheme.themeSource (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts). Code-block colour is a separate control (Code theme, applies in dark mode), so check the code block with Dark.
steps: Click the app menu, then Settings…, or press Command+,.
Click Appearance in the left list.
In the row labelled Theme, click Light. Look: the window, chat and code blocks turn light.
Click Dark, then System. Look: the window follows the choice; with System, change the Mac's appearance in System Settings > Appearance and check the window changes too.
S6.32.where: Settings… > Appearance > Theme > Light, Dark or System

S6.33.needs: none (optional: macOS System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Increase contrast for the System choice)
S6.33.note: High sets data-contrast=more (apps/web/shared/components/AppearancePreferences.tsx), styled in apps/web/app/globals.css. The OS Increase contrast setting is not named in the code, so that route is from macOS, not from this app.
steps: Click the app menu, then Settings…, or press Command+,.
Click Appearance in the left list.
In the row labelled Contrast, open the drop-down and choose High.
Look: text, borders and focus rings look stronger than before. Choose System to return.

S6.34.note: States are set in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx (hover:, active:, focus-visible:, disabled:). The exact button that is disabled depends on the screen.
steps: Move the mouse over a button in the chat or Settings and look for a colour change.
Press and hold the mouse on a button and look for a slight shrink and darker fill.
Press the Tab key until a button has a focus ring, and look for the ring.
Find a button that is greyed out and look that it is faded and cannot be clicked.
S6.34.where: No control. Its effect shows on any button: hover, press, keyboard focus, and disabled.

S6.35.note: Icon file is apps/desktop/electron/resources/icon.icns (set in apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml, line 71). Only one icon file exists in that folder, so the tester cannot check each size. Web tab icons are apps/web/app/favicon.ico and apps/web/app/icon.png. The About item label comes from Electron, not from code (role about in apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts).
steps: Click the first menu in the menu bar, the one named Desktop.
Click the About item (its label is set by Electron and reads About Desktop).
Look: the About panel shows the Desktop icon, name and version.
Look at the Dock: the Desktop app icon is shown there.
S6.35.where: The app menu (first menu, named Desktop) > About Desktop (opens the About panel that shows the app icon); the Dock shows the app icon.
